entries.title: Punishing one to warn another
entries.literal_meaning: Beat the daughter to teach the daughter-in-law.
entries.explanation: One person is punished so that someone else takes the warning. The indirect target is the point of the saying.
entries.meaning_odia: ଦଣ୍ଡ ଜଣଙ୍କୁ ଦିଆଯାଉଛି, କିନ୍ତୁ ଭୟ ଦେଖାଇବା ବା ସତର୍କ କରିବାର ଲକ୍ଷ୍ୟ ଆଉ ଜଣେ।
entries.usage_example: A supervisor publicly rebukes one person while looking at another who made the same mistake. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The household image contains violence against women. Recording it does not endorse that violence or claim every family behaves this way.

entries.title: Deal with the root
entries.odia: ମୂଳୁଁ ମାଇଲେ ଯିବ ସରି, ଦେବଙ୍କ ସଙ୍ଗେ କିପାଁ କଳି
entries.literal_meaning: Destroy it at the root and it will end; why quarrel with the gods?
entries.explanation: The words contrast ending something at its source with quarrelling. Reading this as a call to address the underlying cause is editorial.
entries.meaning_odia: ମୂଳ କାରଣକୁ ହଟାଇଲେ କଥା ସରିବ—ଏମିତି ଏକ ଅର୍ଥ ଏଠାରୁ ନିଆଯାଇପାରେ। ଏହା ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା।
entries.usage_example: Rather than repeatedly arguing over duplicate bookings, a group introduces a shared booking record. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: No originating tale or specific sacred tree is supplied by this dictionary passage. The example does not advocate destruction.
